title: Relations and functions
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No single bank point covers both the vertical line test and f(x) evaluation at Stage 5 depth: the closest NSW card is Year 11 and lacks notation, while the Victorian card has notation but no vertical line test and adds domain and range.

draft.title: Relations and functions
card: A relation links inputs (\(x\) values) to outputs (\(y\) values). A function is a relation that gives exactly one output for each input.
Vertical line test: if any vertical line meets a graph more than once, one input has two outputs, so it is not a function.
Function notation \(f(x)\) means the output for input \(x\). For \(f(x) = 2x + 1\), find \(f(3)\) by putting 3 in place of \(x\).
Worked example: \(f(3) = 2 \times 3 + 1 = 7\). So the input 3 gives the output 7, and the graph passes through \((3, 7)\).
draft.remember: A function has one output for each input. \(f(3)\) is the output when \(x = 3\).

a.q: Which set of \((x, y)\) pairs is NOT a function?
a.why: The input 1 gives two outputs, 4 and 6, so this is not a function. In the pairs where every output is 4, each input still has just one output, so that is a function.
a.clue: Look for an input that appears twice with different outputs.

b.why: Put \(-1\) in for \(x\): \((-1)^{2} - 4 \times (-1) = 1 + 4 = 5\). The tempting answer \(-3\) comes from treating \(-4 \times (-1)\) as \(-4\) and getting \(1 - 4\).
b.clue: Square \(-1\) first, then deal with the sign of the second term.
